title: Standard Precautions for All Patient Care | Infection Control | CDC
content: April 3, 2024 Standard Precautions for All Patient Care What to know Standard Precautions are used for all patient care. They're based on a risk assessment and make use of common sense practices and personal protective equipment use that protect healthcare providers from infection and prevent the spread of infection from patient to patient. Recommendation details Perform hand hygiene. Follow hand hygiene recommendations and training for healthcare providers. Follow guidelines for hand hygiene . Training course for hand hygiene. Clean Hands Count materials . Use personal protective equipment (PPE) whenever there is an expectation of possible exposure to an infectious material. Follow guidelines for isolation precautions . Resources to prevent occupationally-acquired infections . Follow respiratory hygiene/cough etiquette principles. Follow guidelines for isolation precautions . Respiratory Hygiene/Cough Etiquette in Healthcare Settings . Materials for patients , including Cover Your Cough signs. Ensure appropriate patient placement. Follow guidelines for isolation precautions . Properly handle, clean and disinfect patient care equipment and instruments/devices. Clean and disinfect the environment appropriately. Follow guidelines for environmental infection control . Follow guidelines for disinfection and sterilization . Use the toolkit for evaluating environmental cleaning . Handle textiles and laundry carefully. Follow guidelines for environmental infection control . Follow safe injection practices. Wear a surgical mask when performing lumbar punctures. Properly handle needles and review the Sharps Safety for Healthcare Settings workbook . Follow guidelines for isolation precautions . Follow guidelines for infrastructure and routine practices in healthcare personnel . Follow guidelines for epidemiology and control of selected infections transmitted among personnel and patients . Follow NIOSH healthcare worker information . Occupationally-Acquired Infections in Healthcare Settings.
